acceptedWorkstreams.title: Run the first-session test on the connections learners actually have, and note what fails
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Learners join cohorts on mid-range Androids over mobile data, not office wifi. Approach: run the accepted three-task script twice for at least one participant each - once on a stable connection and once throttled to a 3G-like state on a real device - and record what only breaks under real conditions, merged with the consented findings from the main sessions. Tasks: network-condition notes (research), merged findings write-up (content).

acceptedWorkstreams.title: Three-task learner script, piloted once, then 5 short sessions
acceptedWorkstreams.description: Write a 15-minute learner session: three tasks (find this week's announcement, open the assignment file, ask a question in the right place), a consent note and a log sheet that records where each person looked first and how long they took. Pilot it with one colleague, fix unclear wording, then run 5 sessions with real learners invited to a test cohort. Summarise every confusion point by how many of the 5 hit it, with a suggested fix. Tasks: script, consent and log (research), findings report after sessions (research).

upvotes.reason: The same three learner tasks are tested first with a pilot and then with five learners, with consent and a log sheet. That makes the confusion points countable and gives the team concrete fixes.

The goal asks where learners get confused finding announcements, files and a place to ask questions. Testing those same three tasks individually, with consent, a pilot and first-choice/time logs, directly identifies those confusions. Report counts out of five as observations from a small sample, not population estimates; recruit real consenting learners before claiming findings.

The three tasks directly test the goal's announcement, file and question journeys. A short pilot can catch leading instructions before the five consented learner sessions. Recording first choice, completion and confusion frequency yields actionable evidence; present results as five-person observations rather than population statistics, and never invent a participant or session.
